versions.name: Release v0.26.9
versions.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v2 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Skill installation and activation

Skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing Skills more reliable.

- Adds PUT /skills/activation and setUserSkillsActivation to enable or disable 1-100 user Skills in one request, with saved preferences and propagation status. ([#16186](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16186))
- Prepares Skill installation for larger archives by adding disk-based ZIP handling and recovery-backup protection to the installer. ([#16421](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16421))
- Adds daemon API routes for installing large Skill ZIPs by upload or host file path and querying installation receipts after failures. ([#16422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16422))
- Adds TypeScript SDK support for installing Skill ZIPs from File, Blob, bytes, or host path, with attempt IDs and receipt lookup. ([#16423](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16423))
- WebShell can now upload Skill ZIP archives from the Skills page, show daemon limits, and check uncertain installation results. ([#16424](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424))

## Web Shell sessions and composer

Web Shell session titles, Add menu polish, draft preservation, batch deletion, and listSessions pagination fixes improve everyday session management.

- Keeps Web Shell sidebar session titles visible when a transcript is rebuilt, preventing session names from disappearing. ([#16299](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16299))
- Polishes the Web Shell composer Add menu with consistent icons, labels, descriptions, spacing, and improved accessibility for actions and Plan state. ([#16181](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16181))
  ![Main menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/d37bb0579f3c6b212c2a18d76acc59af920279fb/composer-menu-16155/before-dark.png)
  ![Updated production-package menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/d37bb0579f3c6b212c2a18d76acc59af920279fb/composer-menu-16155/after-dark.png)
- WebShell now preserves unsent drafts when ArrowUp or ArrowDown moves through wrapped prompt lines before history navigation. ([#14909](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14909))
- web-shell: batch session deletions at the route limit ([#14637](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14637))
  ![Before bulk deletion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jianyx1/qwen-code/82199691bd3c0e8908df82bbaf5d38a98fb44143/before.png)
  ![After bulk deletion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jianyx1/qwen-code/82199691bd3c0e8908df82bbaf5d38a98fb44143/after.png)
- listSessions pagination no longer skips sessions when multiple session files share the same modification time. ([#16024](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16024))

## Managed agents and sessions

Managed agent automation, durable questions, activation renewals, writer recovery, and history caching improve hosted session reliability and speed.

- managed-agent: support durable structured user questions ([#16433](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16433))
- managed-agent: enable automation by default ([#16448](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16448))
- Managed agent activation renewals now locate the activation lease more efficiently, reducing renewal lookup overhead. ([#16336](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16336))
- Improves managed-agent performance by removing tenant guard locks from native journal snapshot publication. ([#16410](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16410))
- Managed Session history rebuilds now cache message bodies per process, reducing repeated reads and improving performance for hosted turns. ([#16337](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16337))
- HTTP Managed Session writer recovery now keeps a live in-flight renewal grant instead of unnecessarily re-acquiring the writer. ([#16287](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16287))

## GitHub PR automation

Sandboxed /verify can read PR review threads, /autofix-pr refusals expose machine-readable codes, and GitHub inbound recovery retries failed reads.

- The sandboxed /verify round can now see PR review threads, including resolved and outdated threads, so reviewer findings are available during verification. ([#16300](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16300))
- /autofix-pr helper refusals now include a machine-readable refused code and next step on stderr, making failures easier to handle. ([#16238](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16238))
- GitHub inbound recovery now retries after a failed read instead of stopping, so recovered tasks run once the task store becomes readable. ([#16402](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16402))

## Model and provider support

Image input fixes for Llama, LLaVA, Pixtral, Mistral Small, and Qwen VL models plus OCI Generative AI documentation broaden provider coverage.

- Enables image input for Llama 3.2 Vision, Llama 4, LLaVA, Pixtral, and Mistral Small 3.1 and 3.2 models. ([#16311](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16311))
- core: accept images for Qwen VL models under their Ollama names ([#16309](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16309))
- providers: document OCI Generative AI under OpenAI-compatible providers ([#16345](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16345))

## Channels and messaging

QQ proactive delivery and richer Channel event timeline recording improve active group messaging, delivery tracking, and scan health visibility.

- Enables QQ proactive delivery so loop messages, webhook tasks, background responses, and daemon sends can be sent as active group messages. ([#15635](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15635))
- Channel event timeline now records private bound-session deliveries, undelivered events, and scan health outcomes. ([#16237](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16237))

## CLI and terminal status

Interactive CLI reports working, blocked, done, or error status via OSC 7501, while experimental.unifiedAgentLoop helps Ink TUI finish tool batches.

- The interactive CLI now reports working, blocked, done, or error status to terminals using OSC 7501 with app=qwen-code. ([#16407](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16407))
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, Ink TUI turns await their shared tool batch so tool continuations complete within the turn. ([#16385](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16385))

## Daemon, runtime, and account recovery

Faster SSH registration and MCP startup, reduced tool-execution locking, bounded daemon replay memory, and subscription recovery improve platform stability.

- SSH registration settlement and Session worktree preparation are less serialized, allowing more concurrent Runtime work and faster workspace preparation. ([#16386](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16386))
- Loads MCP client Google auth providers on demand to reduce startup load while keeping configured server behavior unchanged. ([#16242](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16242))
- Improves ordinary session tool execution performance by reducing unnecessary locking during admission and dispatch. ([#16415](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16415))
- Daemon command and skill replay now limits snapshot memory with an 8 MiB per-session ring, configurable via --event-ring-max-bytes. ([#16413](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16413))
- subscription: isolate activation and restore sign-in recovery ([#16453](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16453))

## Other Changes

- Internal test coverage for renewal recovery and writer seal handling was hardened without changing production behavior. ([#14482](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14482))
- Consolidates Web Shell sidebar test scaffolding onto a shared sidebarHarness without changing user-visible behavior. ([#16016](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16016))
- Adds a design proposal for moving PR state transition detection from GitHub channel polling to the daemon PR refresh timer. ([#16246](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16246))
- Shortens the stale PR policy to mark pull requests stale after 30 inactive days and close them after 14 more days, with a larger sweep budget. ([#16435](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16435))
- Fixes release Docker integration builds to use the same apt-mirror probe as E2E builds, improving mirror selection and cache reliability. ([#16278](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16278))
- The no-AK integration gate now runs on the self-hosted ECS pool for every pull request, including untrusted forks. ([#16132](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16132))
- test(managed-agent): cover pending sibling approval holds ([#15994](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15994))
- ci: build the PR tree once and shorten the required path ([#16450](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16450))
  ![Screenshot from pull request 16450](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a78d1c35-4957-416a-92aa-e3c642125344)
  ![Screenshot from pull request 16450](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51886ce5-eee8-422e-9a96-03e524b77bbf)

---

## 中文摘要

### Skill 安装与激活

Skill ZIP 上传、daemon API、TypeScript SDK 支持、批量激活与恢复备份保护，让 Skill 安装和管理更可靠。

- 新增 PUT /skills/activation 与 setUserSkillsActivation，可一次启用或禁用 1-100 个用户 Skill，并返回保存与传播状态。 ([#16186](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16186))
- 为大型 Skill 压缩包安装做准备，在安装器中加入从磁盘读取 ZIP 的能力与恢复备份保护。 ([#16421](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16421))
- 新增守护进程 API，可通过上传或主机文件路径安装大型 Skill ZIP，并在失败后查询安装回执。 ([#16422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16422))
- TypeScript SDK 支持通过 File、Blob、字节或主机路径安装 Skill ZIP，并提供尝试 ID 与回执查询。 ([#16423](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16423))
- WebShell 现在可从 Skills 页面上传 Skill ZIP，显示守护进程限制，并查询不确定的安装结果。 ([#16424](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424))

### Web Shell 会话与输入

Web Shell 会话标题、Add 菜单细节、草稿保留、批量删除与 listSessions 分页修复改进日常会话管理。

- 当 transcript 重建时保留 Web Shell 会话列表标题，避免会话名称丢失。 ([#16299](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16299))
- 优化 Web Shell 作曲器 Add 菜单的图标、标签、描述、间距，并改进无障碍展示与 Plan 状态指示。 ([#16181](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16181))
- WebShell 现在在 ArrowUp 或 ArrowDown 浏览换行提示行时保留未发送草稿。 ([#14909](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14909))
- web-shell: batch session deletions at the route limit ([#14637](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14637))
- listSessions 分页在多个会话文件修改时间相同时不再跳过会话。 ([#16024](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16024))

### Managed agent 与会话

Managed agent 自动化、持久用户问题、activation 续期、writer 恢复与历史缓存提升托管会话的可靠性与性能。

- managed-agent: support durable structured user questions ([#16433](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16433))
- managed-agent: enable automation by default ([#16448](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16448))
- Managed agent 激活续期现在能更高效定位 activation lease，降低查询开销。 ([#16336](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16336))
- 通过移除 native journal 快照发布中的 tenant 守卫锁，提升 managed-agent 性能。 ([#16410](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16410))
- Managed Session 历史重建现在按进程缓存消息正文，减少重复读取并提升性能。 ([#16337](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16337))
- HTTP Managed Session 写入方恢复现在会保留有效的在途续期授权，避免不必要重新获取。 ([#16287](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16287))

### GitHub PR 自动化

沙箱 /verify 可读取 PR review threads，/autofix-pr 拒绝输出机器可读代码，GitHub 入站恢复在读取失败后重试。

- 沙箱 /verify 轮次现在可读取 PR review threads，包括已解决和过期讨论，便于验证时参考评审意见。 ([#16300](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16300))
- /autofix-pr 助手拒绝时会在 stderr 输出 refused 代码和 next 步骤，便于自动处理。 ([#16238](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16238))
- GitHub 入站恢复在读取失败后会继续重试，任务存储可读后已恢复任务将运行。 ([#16402](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16402))

### 模型与 Provider 支持

Llama、LLaVA、Pixtral、Mistral Small 与 Qwen VL 图像输入修复，以及 OCI Generative AI 文档扩展 provider 覆盖。

- Llama 3.2 Vision、Llama 4、LLaVA、Pixtral 及 Mistral Small 3.1/3.2 支持图像输入。 ([#16311](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16311))
- core: accept images for Qwen VL models under their Ollama names ([#16309](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16309))
- providers: document OCI Generative AI under OpenAI-compatible providers ([#16345](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16345))

### Channel 与消息

QQ 主动消息投递与更完整的 Channel 事件时间线记录改进群消息、投递跟踪和扫描健康可见性。

- QQ 支持主动消息投递，循环、webhook、后台任务和 daemon 发送可作为主动群消息发出。 ([#15635](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15635))
- Channel 事件时间线现在记录私有绑定会话投递、未投递事件和扫描健康结果。 ([#16237](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16237))

### CLI 与终端状态

交互式 CLI 通过 OSC 7501 报告 working、blocked、done 或 error 状态，experimental.unifiedAgentLoop 帮助 Ink TUI 完成工具批处理。

- 交互式 CLI 现在通过 OSC 7501 向终端报告 working、blocked、done 或 error 状态，并标记 app=qwen-code。 ([#16407](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16407))
- 启用 experimental.unifiedAgentLoop 后，Ink TUI 回合会等待共享工具批处理完成。 ([#16385](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16385))

### Daemon、Runtime 与账户恢复

SSH 注册、MCP 启动、工具执行锁与 daemon 回放内存限制优化，以及 subscription 恢复改进平台稳定性。

- SSH 注册结算与 Session worktree 准备减少串行限制，支持更多并发 Runtime 工作。 ([#16386](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16386))
- 按需加载 MCP 客户端的 Google auth providers，降低启动负载且配置服务器行为不变。 ([#16242](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16242))
- 通过减少普通会话工具执行准入与调度中的不必要锁，提高执行性能。 ([#16415](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16415))
- 守护进程命令和技能回放限制快照内存，默认每会话 8 MiB，可用 --event-ring-max-bytes 配置。 ([#16413](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16413))
- subscription: isolate activation and restore sign-in recovery ([#16453](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16453))

### 其他变更

- 增强续期恢复与 writer seal 的测试覆盖，不改变生产行为。 ([#14482](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14482))
- 将 Web Shell 侧边栏测试脚手架合并到共享 sidebarHarness，不影响用户可见行为。 ([#16016](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16016))
- 新增设计提案，将 PR 状态变化检测从 GitHub 频道轮询迁移到 daemon 的 PR 刷新定时器。 ([#16246](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16246))
- 将 stale PR 策略缩短为 30 天无活动标记、再过 14 天关闭，并提高单次清理预算。 ([#16435](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16435))
- 修复 release Docker 集成构建，使其与 E2E 一样使用 apt-mirror 探测，提升镜像选择与缓存可靠性。 ([#16278](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16278))

versions.name: v5.1.70
versions.body:
**Plain `omo login` signs a computer in from the terminal while OmO accounts are closed.** A computer with no OmO desktop app — a server over SSH, a fresh Linux box — runs `omo login`, gets a device code to approve on another device, and stores the credential in the OS credential store; the attach-before-mint refusal (#13096) answers a computer that already has its device before anything is asked of the service. The success line names the signed-in account (`Signed in to OmO as <email>.`), and `omo whoami` names it too; a failed account read still says how to see it. `omo logout` and `omo whoami` run while closed, so no message names a command that refuses. `login --help` describes the route (the command stays hidden from `omo --help`), every other closed `login` form refuses with a message that names the route, the closed hints name both routes, and the compiled entry classifies bare `login`, `logout` and `whoami` as one-shot launches with the same shared parse the command uses (`login --` included). The damaged-item message names the terminal route too instead of a desktop-app-only dead end. Tests run the flow through the npm launcher (against a service-auth bundle built from this source into a temp copy of the launcher tree), the compiled entry and the toolkit CLI, with an isolated HOME and runtime dir, no inherited session bus, an injected store, and a refusal-text assertion on every zero-mint case. ([#13281](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13281)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))

**The computer-use conformance preflight tests pass on Windows.** The missing-driver message now prints its repo-relative path with forward slashes on every OS, so a run reads the same on every host, and the stdio-probe test builds its stand-in engine as a real executable for the host instead of a POSIX shell script. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13295](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13295), part of #13221)

**Computer use gets a declared-outcome conformance catalog for its QA.** `script/qa/computer/conformance/` adds a typed catalog in which every action, toolkit and mode cell on each OS declares that it delivers or refuses with an exact engine code, a report that fails a missing, duplicate, skipped or mis-coded cell or one that disturbed the person's session, an environment preflight that ends a broken host's run as `ENVIRONMENT_ERROR`, and twelve model-free reference tasks. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13241](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13241), part of #13221)

**The desktop session's actionability wait test no longer fails on a busy host.** The battery's wait now runs on an injectable clock: the host's monotonic time in a session, as before, and the fake backend's own clock in the test. So `the_battery_waits_for_an_element_that_appears_enabled_after_500_ms` checks the 500 ms wait in fake time instead of wall-clock bounds that host load could break. Runtime behaviour does not change. ([#13180](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13180), fixes #13178)

**A fuzzy handoff no longer fails on an account with many ended sessions, and never goes to a different session than an exact name would.** A fuzzy handoff first tries the thread's exact id, alias or name across every session, ended ones on other devices included, so a name that exactly matches one session always reaches that session. Otherwise local, live and ended sessions are compared together and the clearly best match wins wherever it lives; two equally good matches ask you to pick. Ended sessions that cannot match no longer count against the 500-candidate fuzzy cap, so a large history no longer blocks a unique match. ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141), follows #13066)

**A thread whose alias claim asks for a sign-in after it was created is still named by the alias.** When the account token expires between `thread_create` checking an alias and claiming it, the thread it already created is now named by the alias on its device and the call answers `ok` with `alias_scope: "local"`, instead of an error. `thread_rename` does the same when the account is gone by the claim. An alias used as a local name is now trimmed on every path. ([#13179](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13179), follows #13112) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))

**`omo login` no longer registers a second device for a computer that already has one.** Before any code, browser tab or new key, it checks the stored sign-in and the device the computer's OmO device service holds (parked included). A held, uncertain, locked or unreadable state refuses a new device and keeps the existing one, instead of adding an "omo CLI on <host>" row beside the desktop's. When the service advertises machine identity, both sign-in flows send a hashed hardware id (`SHA256("omo-machine-v1" + id)`; the raw id never leaves the computer), and a `machine_exists` refusal ends the sign-in without removing or taking over any device. ([#13096](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13096)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))

**A thread alias no longer blocks thread creation when no account is signed in.** `thread_create` with an `alias` now creates the thread when the alias registry cannot get an account token. A desktop launch is always in that state. The alias becomes the thread's local name unless a `name` is given, and the result says the alias is local only (`alias_scope: "local"`). `thread_rename` with an alias does the same. Every other alias error is unchanged. ([#13112](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13112), fixes #13104)

Fixed: file reads through the bundled bunshin SDK over the relay work again (`readText`, `readBytes` and `read` no longer reject with "truncated must be a boolean for byte results"), an op sent with a minted capability token is no longer refused as malformed, and an unsupported `clientName` now fails at once with `invalid_client_name` naming the supported role. ([#13108](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13108))

**The machine-binding module no longer exports an unused helper.** `deviceProfileOf` from #13095 is now module-private, so the knip dead-code check on dev is green again. No behavior change. ([#13097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13097))

**One computer is one OmO device: omo login binds to the machine's device service instead of registering its own.** A sign-in now advertises machine binding. When the service asks for the machine hash, omo asks this machine's device service (`device.machine_binding`) for it, and computes the same hash itself when no device service runs. The sign-in presents the device keys this machine already holds, so the service keeps the machine's existing device instead of adding a row. If the device service holds a device whose keys omo does not have (the desktop app's sign-in), omo refuses and points to the desktop app instead of minting a second device. The raw OS machine id never leaves the computer. A computer with no readable machine id signs in exactly as before. ([#13095](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13095))

**The programming skill opens with code ownership.** Its first paragraph tells the model it owns the code: fit new behavior into the existing structure, leave no duplicate or dead code, and fix a defect in the code being changed at its root cause instead of excusing it as pre-existing or someone else's. It replaces the "lazy senior engineer" persona line. ([#13091](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13091))

**A monitor no longer loses a batch that arrives while the previous one is being sent.** `flushMonitor` deleted the monitor's pending entry after awaiting a dispatch, so a batch queued during that await vanished without counting as dropped. The flush now deletes the entry only when it is still the one it drained. ([#13089](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13089))

**A foreground task waits for its child instead of failing at once.** Every `task` with `run_in_background: false` ended with `Session error` about a second in and aborted the child, because opencode reports a running assistant turn with `error: null` and the poller treated the key itself as a failure. Only an error that is set ends the child now. ([#13076](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13076))

**The beta channel no longer falls behind the stable release.** Every stable release now also moves `omo-ai@beta` on npm and the `beta` installer channel on get.omo.dev to that release, unless beta already holds a newer prerelease, so `bun add -g omo-ai@beta` and `install.sh beta` never install something older than `latest`. The beta move and its beta >= latest guard now also run when a release is re-run after it was already published, and after the move beta is re-read: a beta someone moved further forward is left alone, while a beta still older than latest or the newest prerelease fails the run with the exact `npm dist-tag add omo-ai@<version> beta` repair command. ([#12987](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12987), [#13148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13148), [#13149](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13149), [#12990](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12990))

- Computer use: the omo `computer` tool now runs through the desktop SDK; omo sessions open with an explicit report mode (sandbox default unchanged). ([#12840](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12840))

### Fixed

- The hashline test project's lockfile now resolves zod 4.6.7, matching the `^4.6.6` its manifest asks for since #13151, so that project no longer installs the zod 4.6.5 affected by GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5. ([#13282](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13282), follows [#13151](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13151)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- `omo remote bootstrap` can install the device service on macOS again. The release check required a macOS signing identity that was still an empty placeholder, so every download was refused as "failed verification"; it now requires the published identity of the notarized release binaries. ([#13237](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13237), fixes [#13229](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13229)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- The browser skill now uses omowright 0.3.1, which brings the fixes merged since 0.3.0: page navigation owns its readiness and keeps committed state, live regions survive snapshots, cleanup failures are reported instead of swallowed, `aria-hidden` is matched case-insensitively, and BrowserSkill's "more than one browser is online" error lists every browser and the `browser` option to pass. ([#13113](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13113)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- `omo remote send` in wait mode stayed silent for as long as its message waited behind a running turn. A queued send now reports its fate at once on stderr (`Queued on <device>/<session> at position N.`) while stdout keeps only the streamed answer. ([#13273](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13273))
- Computer use v3: the write-scope guard now counts `packages/omo-computer-protocol/src/engine-schema.generated.ts`, the file the protocol generator actually writes, as a generated output. A row that changes the engine schema and regenerates the protocol module is no longer reported as writing outside its scope. Repository tooling only; nothing user-visible changes. ([#13249](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13249))
- `thread_create` with no `cwd` now opens the new thread in the calling session's folder instead of the folder the engine process runs in. A thread created from a desktop thread with no project used to land in the home folder, where its link could not be opened and a follow-up `thread_send` needed `all_scope`. An explicit `cwd` still wins, and a thread created on another device keeps that device's own default. ([#13125](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13125)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))
- From senpi 2026.11.10-3: the footer names the account actually serving the session when the pinned account is blocked, pinned Ultrafast variants no longer warn that Ultrafast is undocumented, provider error text is value-redacted in the model configuration error event, the assistant message and the transcript, every fallback-log field goes through redaction, and after a mid-session model switch the context usage no longer shows the previous model's token count against the new model's window. ([#13109](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13109)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))
- From senpi 2026.11.11 and 2026.11.12: startup no longer fails when the agent's extensions directory is read-only (a sandboxed review child), Claude connection tests keep the redacted provider error and HTTP status and bind each result to the credential they tested, `show_html_page` called from an eval cell is refused instead of silently reaching no reader, and task hosts started from the compiled binary no longer exit with `EBADF` seconds after spawn. ([#13109](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13109)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))
- `computer-v3-guards --residue` now reports a dangling symlink left at a class A or class B removal path. It used to count the broken link as absent and exit 0. ([#13099](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13099), fixes #13065)
- Standalone `omo update` now installs the release instead of printing a curl command (#13084). It downloads the matching platform asset from get.omo.dev with GitHub fallback, verifies published SHA256SUMS and the existing macOS signature, stages beside the installed executable, and keeps a rollback copy until the installed `--version` succeeds. Failures report a typed error; an unwritable directory is refused without partial files. Windows rollback files still held by a running process are cleaned on a later launch. `--dry-run` and `--print` remain print-only. ([#13087](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13087))
- Interrupted standalone updates recover dead or expired install locks without removing a successor's lock. Cleanup failures still release the lease, and symlink launchers update their targets while preserving the links. ([#13087](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13087))
- Count prompt-cache writes when deciding whether to compact and when reporting used and remaining context, so cold-cache turns do not leave tool-output truncation with an inflated context budget. Context-used reporting continues to include generated output tokens. ([#13083](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13083))
- Thread names on other devices now resolve when their sessions are resumable, and fuzzy handoff searches the account's remote candidates as well as local candidates. ([#13066](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13066))
- Failed lookups through a configured relay return their typed error (`host_unavailable` with the device-service state: offline, connecting, keychain locked, authorization stale, degraded or update required); a relay that is not set up (not configured, disabled, signed out, sign-in required) preserves local address resolution. Renaming a remote thread checks names on its own device before changing its name or alias. ([#13066](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13066))
- ast-grep skill: the smoke tests (`tests/smoke.sh`, `tests/smoke.ps1`) pass the search path before `--lang`, the order the skill's own recipes require, and the recipes now say which Python versions reject the other order (3.9 and 3.12 reject it; 3.13+ accept both) instead of naming only 3.9. ([#12714](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12714), thanks @cynkai)

### Changed

- `omo login --new-device` is gone. The OmO service keeps one device per computer, so registering another device over an unreadable stored sign-in either failed after approval or left two live devices. When the stored sign-in cannot be read, `omo login` gives one recovery: remove this computer's device on the Devices page if it is still listed, then run `omo account forget` (which also has the device service forget the device), then sign in again. When the device service holds the device, it also names that device and says these steps sign out the device service, and the OmO desktop app if it is installed, on this computer. ([#13276](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13276)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- When the credential store is locked, `omo login` says to unlock it and try again. ([#13276](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13276)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- When the device service is installed but does not answer, `omo login` names the service's leftover endpoint file and says that opening the OmO desktop app starts the service. ([#13276](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13276)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- `omo login`'s refusals no longer suggest `omo logout`, which does not work while OmO accounts are closed. A sign-in with an unknown refresh outcome first points to sharing the sign-in from the OmO desktop app when a device service holds this computer's device, and gives the start-over steps only as the fallback, with what they also end. When no device service holds the device, it gives the start-over steps directly. ([#13276](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13276)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- The standalone omo binary stages every package its eval extension needs that the engine does not provide, so the eval tool loads in the binary on senpi 2026.11.13 and later (#13358). ([#13358](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13358)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- The EQ.omo linux-x64 goldens are re-recorded at senpi 2026.11.13 (follow-up to #13328) (#13341). ([#13341](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13341)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))
- One protocol doc and one web test fixture describe the private desktop app instead of naming its repository. No behaviour changes. ([#13326](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13326))

The root `knip.ts` composes `knip.base.jsonc` (global settings) with one `knip.workspace.jsonc` per directory (a workspace's config, the root entries under that directory and its pre-existing export rows), so two PRs for two packages no longer conflict on one shared `knip.jsonc`. ### Added

- A Windows live tier for computer use measures, on the hosted Windows runner, whether it can carry five live legs (an elevated target, a locked and a disconnected session, a mixed-DPI second monitor, the elevation prompt's secure desktop) and records the answers in `crates/omo-computer-backend-win32/probes/hosted-windows-live.tsv`. The elevated and mixed-DPI legs run there; the other three are recorded for an owned Windows guest. ([#13233](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13233), part of [#13221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13221))
- The senpi `contextFiles.globalPath` setting loads the global context file from an explicit file or directory (for example `~/.agents/AGENTS.md`). It is read from global settings only, and an unset value keeps the current behavior. ([#13109](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13109)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))
- Computer use v3: the engine's result and error contract lands in `omo-computer-core`: `Disposition` with exactly the seven valid `(delivery, retry)` pairs, `ActionReport` with receipts decided by verb (a value verb is `confirmed` only on a read-back equal to what it requested, a pointer or key verb only on an OS-level consumption receipt), wire validation that refuses an overclaiming report, and the one `COMPUTER_*` table keyed by `(engineCode, data.reason)`, total over the closed engine codes and every reason the design emits, checked against a cited inventory of the design. Backend refusals and exec replies now resolve through it. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. ([#13117](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13117))
- Computer use v3: the engine's contract root lands in `omo-computer-core` (the method table with host-only methods split by peer kind, `engine.hello` with `generation`, `limits` and `machineId`, the `computer.*` settings table, the enumerated environment seams, the untrusted-text listing records and the refusing `Backend` / `AxBackend` traits), with the generated engine schema and protocol doc and the generated `@oh-my-opencode/omo-computer-protocol` types and call-chain classifier. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. ([#13107](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13107))
- Interactive standalone release launches now check and install updates asynchronously through the same verified updater, at most once per UTC day. Background diagnostics go to the canonical agent directory's `auto-update.log` without disturbing the terminal. Offline mode and `OMO_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` (including legacy Senpi/Pi equivalents) disable this startup check. Maintainer builds, headless commands and directly invoked provisioned runtime copies never auto-update. ([#13087](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13087))
- Computer use v3: the new engine workspace is registered as empty building units (10 `omo-computer-*` crates, 7 `@oh-my-opencode/omo-computer-*` packages), with a `bun run test:computer` script and the `computer native contract` CI matrix on macOS, Linux and Windows. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. ([#13028](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13028))

### Security

- Desktop memory sync no longer risks running out of memory on an oversized reply from the sync service. zod moves to 4.6.7 (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5: validating a huge array collected one issue per bad element), and every array the sync channel reads is now capped at 100,000 items, so an oversized reply is rejected up front. This release pins senpi 2026.11.13. versions.body:
**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.10-2.** A client can read and edit the workspace's instruction files over RPC through `read_project_file` / `write_project_file` (senpi#6307), a built session can be parked and handed out through `claim_session` (senpi#6350), the Fable 5.2 prompt preset gains the codebase-ownership sentence (senpi#6360), `generate_image` is eval-only like `bash` (senpi#6272), eval cells reach every eval-only tool through `tool.<name>(...)` and the `agent()`/`output()` helpers (senpi#6276), and the EQ goldens carry the new prompt (senpi#6355). ([#13054](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13054))

**An agent that answered a message from another agent can keep answering it in the turns the engine starts on its own, with no prompt.** The reply allowance a consumed delivery grants (a reply to that sender by id or stated name, approved from the delivery alone) now lasts for the work the delivery started: the consuming turn and every later turn the engine starts by itself - an open-todo reminder, a goal continuation, a monitor wake. A settle alone no longer ends it; it ends when a new message starts work after that answer: a person's message, or any delivery, whose own sender the new group then holds (a delivery that joins running work adds its sender). A reply in a covered turn continues the delivery's chain at the next hop, so the chain limit still closes it. ([#13042](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13042), part of #12996) ([#13044](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13044))

**`omo remote send` now goes through the same delivery pipeline as every other send, and `--steer` reads the session once.** A person's message to a session on another device enters `createDeliveryPipeline` with the relay address book's reference for the `<device>/<session>` address, so the CLI no longer builds its own transport call; the relay transport reads the running turn once and steers it, where the CLI used to read it a second time first. A `--steer` to a session that is running nothing still sends nothing. The unused second prompt implementation (`promptRemote`) and its argument check are removed. Which sender kinds each device admits is unchanged. ([#13038](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13038))

**A message to a session on this device that waits on a question now says so, as one to another device does.** The send is still queued, and its `delivery` now carries `waiting_on: { kind: "approval", device }`. `device` is this install's account device, and is absent when the install has no device identity. ([#13035](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13035))

**Every message one session sends another now names the device it was sent from, on this device and across devices alike, and a message from another device counts as the cause of the receiving run's next send the same way a local one does.** When no device id can be read (no device service, or it does not answer), the message still goes and records why it names no device. ([#13034](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13034), part of [#13004](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13004))

**A message sent or handed off to a session on another device now reports its `delivery_id`, `effective_mode` and `endpoint`, as one sent within this device does.** The answer came from the account's session listing and dropped those fields. It now passes the relay transport's own delivery facts through. The `endpoint` is `null` because the sender knows no endpoint on that device. ([#13033](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13033))

**A reply to an agent on another device now reaches it by the id in the message header or by its name, with no prompt on the same account.** One resolver now finds a thread across this device's threads and the account's other devices: an exact durable id, then an account alias, then the name ladder judged over every entry (two devices sharing a name are an ambiguous_target naming both devices, never a silent pick). `thread_send`, `thread_handoff`, the control tools, `thread_create` (open or fork) and the `omo thread` CLI all use it. A reply to the sender of a delivery the run took in is approved from that delivery alone - by the sender's durable id or the name it stated - and must resolve to that sender, else it is refused as `reply_target_mismatch` without sending. The id shown for a thread on another device is its durable id; the relay listing carries it when the device publishes one. The `omo remote` verbs still dispatch by the id you type as the device's session key, so pass the id the device lists under until that path moves onto the shared resolver. ([#13000](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13000))

**A send to an agent on another device now reports the same facts as one on this device.** `thread_send` and `thread_handoff` answer `delivery_id` and `effective_mode` for a target on another device too, so a caller reads the delivery's id and the lane it took the same way whichever device holds the thread; `message_seq` and `endpoint` stay the facts of a gateway row on this device, and `device` names another one. The reply allowance (a run answering the agent whose delivery it took in, by that agent's id or stated name, with no prompt) is proved identical for a same-device and a cross-device delivery, and one parity table now runs every send assertion against both legs, so a rule that reads the transport fails the build instead of reaching a user. ([#13006](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13006), on top of [#13000](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13000))

**A task child no longer starts against a senpi engine that refused its process-wide redaction registry; the start fails with `SenpiEngineRestartRequiredError`, which says to restart omo.** The engine refuses to load next to a registry slot it did not install, and that refusal lasts for the whole process, so a restart is the only remedy. ([#12991](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12991))

**omo now installs the signed device service 0.1.27 instead of 0.1.3.** The device service pin had stayed at 0.1.3 across every device-service release since 0.1.3, and an installed omo only replaces a service older than its pin, so no machine received a newer one. ([#12981](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12981))

**The `thread_*` tools are now eval-only, like `bash`: when an eval tool is present they are no longer in the model's direct tool list and are called as `tool.thread_*()` inside an eval cell.** Behaviour, permissions and results are unchanged, and without eval they stay ordinary direct tools. ([#12907](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12907), closes [#12903](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12903))

**A long-running engine keeps reclaiming crashed one-shot memory runs.** The memory component's cleanup of abandoned one-shot runs, which runs once per engine process outside session opens, now repeats once a day in an engine that stays up, such as the desktop's or a daemon host's, instead of waiting for a restart. ([#12899](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12899))

**Opening a session no longer re-sweeps the memory root.** The memory component's cleanup of abandoned one-shot runs now runs once per engine process, shortly after the first open, instead of inside every session open. A session that ends before that cleanup starts hands it to the next open, so crashed runs are still reclaimed. ([#12896](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12896))

### Fixed

- The senpi barrel load-failure test imported the barrel by a pathname-derived `/D:/...` specifier, which failed on Windows and turned dev red (#13068). It now imports the barrel by file URL. ([#13068](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13068))
- Computer use reports a click or typed text that went out as window events with its real input route, and judges whether input landed only for multi-event input such as drags, so a single click whose window then closes is reported delivered. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- The actionability check no longer refuses `press` on a Linux button that lists only another action such as `click`, since the backend presses its first action. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Computer use flags text typed into a secure field of a background window, and reports how much text was delivered when the user intervenes mid-send. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- On macOS, key priming now bounds and classifies its focus reads, so a slow or failing focus read no longer stalls background typing into a multi-window app. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Computer use keeps holding the machine-wide interaction lock while it hands key focus back after background typing, so another session can no longer type in between. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- A steer sent to a session on another device that was held behind that session's open draft, and whose turn ended before the draft was released, was answered `queued` and then lost without a word (#12927). The send now records that refusal: a retry of the same send under the same `idempotency_key` answers `turn_conflict`, naming the delivery, instead of `queued`. ([#12935](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12935))

### Changed

- Computer use now lets the user keep typing and clicking while it works by default (`computer.intervention: "continue"`); set it to `"pause"` to have input wait for the user and stop with `UserIntervened`. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- While computer use waits for an accessibility target to become actionable, other computer-use sessions of the same user can keep sending input instead of being refused `InputBusy`; the target is checked once more, without waiting, right before the action. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Desktop engine: the stop-marker policy is pinned to the XPC-only path and reported by `omo doctor`. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))

### Added

- Computer use waits until an accessibility target is actionable before it acts, lists the sheets, windows and menus an action opened, suggests the next call when it refuses, and refuses `cmd+q`, `alt+f4` and `win+l` unless the key chord is forced. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Wayland (Hyprland): window-targeted pointer input through libei behind a `windowInput` capability probe (`no_eis`, `hyprland_ipc_missing` reasons). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Wayland (KWin): window-targeted pointer input through the same libei path, and window captures placed on the KWin frame rectangle so coordinates round-trip between capture and click. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- `senpi-desktop-sdk`: the typed facade package for computer-use v2 consumers (connect, Computer / Window / Element / Frame, reports and verification, typed errors), with a pinned facade manifest and a package-boundaries test. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: `skeleton` observation (logical depth 3), the web-wrapper rule, and `root: <ref>` drill with sub-generations (object mode only). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- `senpi-desktop-sdk`: the spawn transport with the in-session refusal (`spawn_inside_session`); the service run facade routes windows, displays and capabilities through the SDK. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine host: features-gated session.open options (intervention, macosKeyPriming, trace, reportMode) sent only when the engine advertises them; `ActionReport` typed exec results with the 7 valid disposition pairs; reserved settings `computer.run_sandbox`, `intervention`, `macos_key_priming`, `trace` (defaults unchanged); error codes `COMPUTER_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`, `COMPUTER_CAPTURE_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `COMPUTER_PROTECTED_PROCESS` with `data.reason` hints. versions.body:
**`omo thread` says when a broken install leaves it on this device only.** A thread client sidecar that cannot be loaded no longer makes `omo thread read <alias>` silently answer `not_found`: stderr names the sidecar, the error, and the reinstall step. The CLI sign-in's own warnings (a retired trust pin, a failed device-service forget) now reach stderr too. ([#12936](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12936))

**A message to a busy thread now reaches the turn it is running, by default.** `thread_send` and `thread_handoff` with no delivery mode (and `omo thread send` without `--mode`) steer the recipient's running turn and start a turn when it is idle, on this device and on another device alike; a message queues behind the running turn only when the caller asks for `follow_up`, or when the turn cannot take a steer (a waiting question, a compaction, an engine that reports no turn epoch). A send that steers a turn ending at that very moment falls back to the lane the target has then instead of failing. ([#12921](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12921), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9-2.** A tool that an eval cell awaits no longer leaves the running cell blank for a moment when it finishes: its streamed lines stay until the cell's own output or its result replaces them (senpi#6257). ([#12920](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12920))

**`omo remote send` now travels the same road as a session's `thread_send` to another device, and every reply from another device is explained by one mapping.** The person at a terminal who sends to a session on another device goes through the relay transport (the same offline check, the same steer preflight against the running turn, a receipt in this device's gateway store) while keeping their own prompt record; what the user reads when a command on another device is refused (`omo remote`, the attach TUI, the thread tools and the SDK) comes from a single module, so a device that did not answer, a missing grant or an uncertain result reads the same everywhere. ([#12911](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12911), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12885](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12885))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9.** It brings senpi's `admit_external_message` (a message relayed from another device's session is admitted as an ordinary delivery) and makes a relayed delivery read exactly like a same-machine one, with the device kept in its metadata only. The one-channel relay transport (#12879) needs both. ([#12904](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12904))

**The Install button on omo.dev's header no longer presses against or slips past the pill's right edge.** The floating nav bar gives its last control the same inset as the logo on the left, and below 1000 px the section links move into the menu so nothing is pushed outside the pill in any language. ([#12893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12893))

**A thread an agent creates or forks with `thread_create` now starts in the creator's own approval mode on this device too, not the host's default.** A session created on another device already did (#6189); the two legs now run one body: a name is checked against the device the thread lands on (a name that device already lists live is `name_conflict` there), opening a thread that is live on another device answers that thread without opening it again, and the created thread's facts (name, working directory, timestamps) come from the engine's reply on both devices. ([#12891](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12891), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**Stopping, closing, renaming, re-modelling, changing the reasoning level of, or reading a thread works the same way whether that thread runs on this machine or on another device of your account.** `thread_set_reasoning` now reaches a thread on another device too, and a session with no file yet that another client still holds answers the same on both. ([#12890](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12890), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message an agent sends to a session on another device now arrives there exactly as a message between sessions on one device.** The receiving session gets a delivery entry (never a user message) with the same sender line and authority notice a same-device delivery carries, deduplicated under the same key, and it wakes on receipt the same way; a reply is just another send back. Nothing in the delivered text names the device it crossed, and `omo remote send` from a terminal is unchanged. A send from `omo thread send` to a session on another device is refused as data (the engine admits a command-line delivery only from its own machine) and points at `omo remote send`. ([#12889](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12889), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12882](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12882), fixes [#12877](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12877), fixes [#12346](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12346), fixes [#12865](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12865), fixes [#12857](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12857))

**Sending a message to another session now goes through one delivery pipeline whether that session is on this machine or on another device.** The device difference is a transport module behind one port; nothing a user sees changes in this release. ([#12887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12887), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message to a session on another device now reads exactly like one from a session on the same machine.** The receiving agent sees which session sent it, not which device, and replies by that session as usual. ([#12878](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12878))

**A subagent whose model takes more than 90 s to start answering is no longer aborted by runtime fallback.** With `runtime_fallback` enabled, the first-prompt watchdog cut every subagent that showed no progress within a fixed 90 s and re-prompted the fallback model, so reasoning-heavy models that legitimately think longer before their first token were killed and their prompt was sent twice. The watchdog now waits 300 s, the same stream-start bound the engines use, and `runtime_fallback.first_prompt_timeout_seconds` sets it (`0` disables it). ([#11893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11893), fixes [#11887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11887))

### Fixed

- `omo thread send` to a thread alias held on this device now reaches that thread when run from another workspace, the same way `omo thread read` does, instead of answering that no visible thread matches. ([#12860](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12860))
- Memory shutdown drain: the session-shutdown wiring no longer claims senpi puts no bound on its handler. senpi bounds one `session_shutdown` handler with its own warn threshold, per-handler timeout and total quit budget (shipped defaults 2 s / 10 s / 2 s, each user-tunable and 0-disableable), and the 1500 ms drain budget is sized under those defaults and pinned by a test that reads them from the installed senpi, so a host release that lowers a default below the drain fails there. No host cap was added from OmO and nothing bypasses the host abort; a journal flush skipped by the budget still raises its error-level alarm. ([#12795](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12795), refs [#10336](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10336))
- The browser skill's docs and examples teach BrowserSkill 0.4 shared control for the omowright it now ships (`^0.3.0`): every gated page action carries the context of a fresh `session.cooperate("sync")`, and a `cooperation_sync_required` refusal waits for the person with `session.cooperate("wait")`, then re-syncs and replans. They also note which calls are gated, that a gated action throws a `TypeError` on an unknown option key (with the two calls that pass stray keys through instead), and that `page.on("dialog")` listeners receive a `Dialog` they can answer. The omowright this release ships includes running-browser discovery through `DevToolsActivePort`, `goto` on sparse and frameset pages, UTF-8 decoding across BrowserSkill IPC chunks and unique-only stale-ref recovery (thanks @ashmoonori-afk, code-yeongyu/omowright#115 to #118), and agent tabs in their own window (thanks @devxoul, code-yeongyu/omowright#120). ([#12494](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12494))
- The senpi-task cold-revive residency test is now bounded by the product's own liveness rules instead of a flat 20 s total (Part of #10993). A Windows child that blocks for a while during startup no longer fails it unless the product would also give up, and a real stall fails with the last stage it reached and the stall length. The test's child also reports senpi's startup phase timings, so the next block names its phase. ([#11706](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11706))

### Changed

- Skills: `ulw-research` and mass research in `mass-ulw` now require every conclusion to rest on something a tool actually observed. Workers tag claims `OBSERVED:` and dead ends `PROBED:`, anything known only from memory is sent back as a lead, and mass-research verify nodes re-open each observed source. Both research editions state the rule in their opening contract, and every mass-ulw node prompt carries it in its VERIFY item. ([#12832](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12832), fixes [#12830](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12830))

versions.name: v5.1.65
versions.body:
**A message an agent sends to a session on another device now says who sent it.** It used to arrive there as plain text, indistinguishable from that session's own user. It now carries the same sender line and authority notice as a message between sessions on one device (the sending session, its workspace and project, and the device it came from), and a leading `/` in it no longer runs a command or expands a prompt template on the receiving side. `omo remote send` from a terminal is unchanged. ([#12858](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12858), part of [#12852](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12852))

**Memory retention no longer evaluates its completion-record guard twice per record.** The completion sweep now reads the guard once and keeps or removes the record on that single answer, and the retention tests check their own preconditions instead of asserting them away. No change to what retention keeps or removes. ([#12783](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12783), follow-up to [#12532](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12532))

**The standalone `omo` binary's `omo doctor` reports memory runtime size again, like the npm install.** Each memory identity's runtime size against its cap and the total across identities are printed by both distributions, so binary/npm doctor parity holds ([#12785](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12785)). ([#12783](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12783))

**Old binary runtimes are pruned safely when two `omo` launches start at once.** A launch no longer deletes a runtime another launch is still pruning, and a runtime that launch already removed is not reported as a failure. `omo --version`, `--help` and `omo update` never prune. ([#12770](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12770), follow-up to [#12627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12627))

**A task child whose engine cannot hold its designated model chain is no longer started.** Before, when a process child's engine could not take its chain (an older engine, a refused `set_retry_fallback`, or no answer in time) or a task host did not advertise `retry_fallback_profile`, the child was still prompted and ran on the engine's own fallback settings, which can reach models outside its chain. The start now fails before the first prompt and names every designated model and the reason, and such a host is refused as incompatible, naming the same models. ([#12759](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12759)) ([#12761](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12761))

**A command on a closed session on another device now reports the same error as on this device.** It answered `session_not_found` remotely and `unknown_session` locally; both now answer `unknown_session`. ([#12755](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12755)) ([#12756](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12756))

**omo hands its device keys to the device service from memory, with no credential store read for relay.** A fresh sign-in (`omo login`, `omo account adopt`) deletes the signed-out marker and then hands its in-memory keys and account to a running device service. The memory sync session re-adopts from the credential it already holds when the service reports no adopted device. Every sign-out path (logout, forget, a session the service ended) tells the service to forget the device. The start-up bootstrap no longer reads the stored credential. `device.adopt` carries `account` only to a device service at 0.1.3 or newer, and the pinned device service is raised to 0.1.3 (design D PR 4). ([#12735](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12735))

**`omo remote` can open, send, switch model, interrupt and close sessions on your other devices.** `omo remote open <device> [--project P] [--model M]` starts a session there and prints `<device>/<session>`; `omo remote send <device>/<session> <text>` prints the answer as it streams in and returns when the turn settles (`--steer` steers the running turn, `--follow-up` queues behind it, `--no-wait` returns once the session took the message); `model`, `interrupt` and `close` do what they say. Each verb is the same remote op the agent's thread tools use, and `--json` prints its typed result. A steer to a session on another device now reaches it when that device's engine reports its running turn, instead of always being refused. ([#12709](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12709), part of [#12320](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12320))

Creating or forking a thread on another device no longer waits for a separate `session.locate` round trip: the create asks the relay for the new session's id on the `open_session` reply and uses it. A relay daemon without that answer (an older host, or an older service on this device) is handled as before, with `session.locate`. ([#12686](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12686))

**`omo update` on the standalone binary now replaces the installed `omo`.** It used to print a replace command for the copy under `~/.omo/binary-runtime/<version>/`, which the next launch put back, so the update never took. A launch also removes old runtime versions there, keeping the previous one for a rollback and any version still running. ([#12627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12627), fixes [#12626](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12626))

**Each memory identity's runtime directory is capped at 2 GiB, and `omo doctor` and `/doctor` show how much it holds.** After retention, the 12-hour memory maintenance pass evicts oldest-first until the identity fits `memory.runtime.max_bytes` (default 2 GiB, `0` for unbounded, per-agent overridable under `memory.agents.<id>.runtime`). It removes folded reflection runs first, then the transcripts of fully reflected sessions, idle sidecars, and finally old failed runs beyond the newest ten. Journals that were never or only partly reflected are kept by default; `memory.runtime.discard_unreflected_journals: true` lets the cap evict them too, and only while reflection is succeeding on the identity. Live sessions, in-flight runs and the run-id high water are never touched. `omo doctor` prints each identity's runtime size and the total, and warns when an identity reaches 80 % of its cap. `/doctor` adds a `runtime-size` check with the largest stores and what retention would still free. ([#12538](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12538))

**Memory no longer grows without bound on disk.** The background memory maintenance pass now removes finished reflection runs, fully reflected transcripts, recall sidecars and legacy stores past configurable windows (`memory.runtime.retention_days` 7, `completions_days` 30), in time-boxed slices that resume where they stopped. Transcript input reflection never folded into memory is kept unless you turn on `discard_unreflected_journals` (then removed after `abandoned_journal_days`, 14, only while reflection works for that agent). Nothing a live session owns, no locked or unfinished work and no run id reflection still needs is touched. ([#12532](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12532))

A reflection lock left behind by a run whose processes died (launcher killed before the run started, supervisor and child gone with no outcome, an unreadable run ledger, or a torn `active.lock`) is now released at session start, on the next turn, and by the new `omo doctor --fix` (`--dry-run` to preview, `/doctor --fix` in a session), instead of keeping every later reflection queued; `omo doctor --fix` also reclaims runtime locks whose owner is gone. ([#12517](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12517))

### Fixed

- Senpi: omo now names any senpi feature it relies on that the running senpi lacks in one startup warning, and opening a monitor on another device's session on a senpi without remote wake fails with `remote_wake_unavailable` instead of starting a watch that never wakes. A contract test checks every such feature against the pinned senpi. ([#12862](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12862), fixes [#12861](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12861))
- The browser skill now depends on the published `omowright` package (`^0.3.0`, the first release that ships a built `dist/` that loads under Node as well as Bun) instead of a git commit. Its runtime stager and loader accept omowright's TypeScript sources, the older JavaScript sources, or a compiled `dist/`, in that order, so a future layout change cannot silently break the staged browser runtime (#12842, #12851, #12847). ([#12847](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12847))
- Memory facts extraction records facts again with senpi 2026.11.6-3: the facts child (also used by onboarding's understand step) keeps the approval mode its own settings give it and may run only its own record tools without asking, instead of being refused as a child whose parent is gone. ([#12839](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12839))
- Concurrent memory account resolves on a desktop host share one open, so the app sees one `descriptor` request instead of one per caller; a failed open is retried by the next resolve (carried from #12717, which this PR supersedes). ([#12839](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12839))
- Thread tools: an agent can now reach a session on another device of the same account by its name. A name that matches the title of one live session on another device sends there, and a name shared across devices (or with a thread on this device) is refused as ambiguous with every candidate and its device listed, never picked silently. Claiming or renaming a thread alias on a signed-in CLI device now reaches the account's alias registry instead of always answering that the registry cannot be reached; an alias claimed on one device now reaches that thread from every other device instead of reporting its device offline, and a registry outage never changes how a plain name resolves. `omo thread read` resolves aliases and other devices' threads the way the agent's `thread_read` does. ([#12837](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12837), fixes [#12833](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12833))
- Release: the service-auth release step now refuses a bundle that carries more than one release key set, so it always checks the set the bundle ships. ([#12812](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12812), fixes [#12617](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12617))
- Runtime fallback: when a session times out and no fallback model can be prepared, the user is now warned even if nothing was awaiting a fallback, the warning names the real reason ("no available fallback models" while attempts remain, instead of "max fallback attempts reached"), and a compaction that outlives its watchdog budget returns control as a real cancellation without staying marked as recovering. ([#12790](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12790), fixes [#12762](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12762))
- Standalone binary on Windows: running the provisioned runtime copy directly (`~/.omo/binary-runtime/<version>/omo.exe`) no longer hands off to itself and reports itself as the installed launcher when the home path is spelled with an 8.3 short name or different letter case. ([#12772](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12772), fixes [#12769](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12769))
- While service accounts are closed, the compiled `omo` binary recognises the device-code `omo login` with the same option parse as the command itself, so `omo login -- --device` and similar argv get the immediate refusal instead of being handed on to the command. ([#12723](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12723), fixes [#12646](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12646))
- The browser skill's doctor no longer calls a browser ready when its only BrowserSkill extension is 0.4.0. That release left a "BrowserSkill" tab group in the user's browser after every task. The doctor now reports `outdated-extension` and tells the user to update the extension and delete the saved groups. ([#12663](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12663))
- `omo` no longer warns "Could not download the OmO device service. Check the connection and try again." on every interactive start while the device service release it pins has not been published. A 404 for that release is now its own `not_published` state: the start stays quiet, and `omo remote bootstrap` says remote devices are not available in this build yet. A connection failure, a server error or a half-published release still warns. ([#12659](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12659))
- When a dream or reflection run deletes, archives or moves a memory note, `[[path]]` and relative markdown links to it in other notes are now updated in the same run, after the completion check has decided which of the run's changes land. A moved note's links follow it, and the moved note's own relative links keep pointing at their targets. A note the run archived, meaning its `ARCHIVE.md` entry names the file (its path, or its file name when no other note shares it), is linked as `[[ARCHIVE.md|<old path> (archived)]]`. Links to any other removed note, such as one the user asked to forget, become plain text. A note the completion check refuses, or one whose rewrite it would refuse (for example a note that already holds secret-like text), or one that is not valid UTF-8, keeps its links as they were, so `/doctor` can still report those. A targeted `/dream --to <doc>` that removes its own target is no longer refused because of these link updates. Facts extraction also no longer writes into a month ledger path that was archived or deleted: that month's new facts go to `notes/facts/<month>-2.md` (then `-3`, ...), so an old link can never start pointing at unrelated new content. ([#12642](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12642)) ([#12645](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12645))
- Runtime fallback keeps compaction retries separate from the primary model chain and preserves substantive retry prompts. Compaction watchdogs defer within a bounded budget, exhausted native retry signals do not trigger an abort, and stuck-session watchdogs still return control when no replacement can be dispatched. Thanks @mradwankhalil. ([#11907](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11907), fixes [#9786](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9786))
- Background tasks let runtime fallback decide who recovers a session error before starting a replacement or finalizing the task. Exhausted and refused retries release recovery ownership, model-less retry errors can finish the task, and a slow decision never starts a competing replacement. ([#9683](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9683), [#11907](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11907))
- Runtime fallback keeps its place in the fallback chain when its own abort echoes back as a stop or idle event, and no longer mistakes its own retry for a manual model change. A failing fallback now moves on to the next model instead of going back to the model that just failed. ([#11901](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11901), fixes [#6751](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/6751))
- Runtime fallback: a session timeout whose fallback dispatch is rejected now uses up the attempt, stops at `max_fallback_attempts`, and ends with an abort the caller sees instead of re-arming the timer forever. ([#11898](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11898), fixes [#6637](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/6637))
- First-prompt refusal tests now await launch settlement when the bounded start report arrives first, preserving both untyped and non-credential refusal diagnostics without depending on subprocess startup speed (#11732). ([#11852](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11852))

### Changed

- Task children ask through the parent session instead of being refused: a child's permission prompt (and its other select, confirm, input and editor dialogs) is raised on the parent's UI, so Allow runs the child's call and Deny does not. A child the parent turn is waiting on asks on the connection that started that turn; a background child asks every attached client that may answer. Secret inputs and permanent grant selections are never forwarded. Children in their own process or on the task host open in the parent's approval mode and follow every later change of it, one change at a time and always ending on the latest; a child that could not follow is reported to the parent session. ([#12839](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12839))
- `omo remote open` and the thread tools' create and fork on another device name the approval mode the new session runs in: the creating session's own mode, or for `omo remote open` the new `--permission-preset` flag, else this device's own setting; a setting that cannot be read is a usage error rather than the loosest mode. ([#12839](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12839))
- The compiled engine no longer has the unused `installEngineCaTrust` startup routine. That routine set `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` but had no caller, and engine launches set up certificate trust in the launcher trust stage. A new test checks that an engine started without `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` in its environment does not get it from the launcher. Validation of `OMO_EXTRA_CA_CERTIFICATES` is unchanged. ([#12628](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12628), part of #10762)

versions.body:
**Desktop memory sync now starts as soon as the engine boots, without waiting for a session.** An engine started by `omo host ensure` loads extensions only when a session opens, while the desktop opens none until the engine has sent the memory-sync bootstrap handshake, so the two waited on each other. The compiled `omo` and the npm launcher now start that one claim before the engine loads whenever an RPC engine's launch declares a `memory-sync` channel; the first session reuses it. A claim that fails still reports memory sync as unavailable and never falls back to CLI credentials. ([#12702](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12702)) ([#12704](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12704))

Internal (tests only): macOS trust acquisition reads `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` through the already-injectable bundle reader, and a test now proves that a malformed default file yields the structured `openssl-default-file-malformed` drop entry (file, cause, block index, narrowing).
